questions.q: A play set in pre-colonial Kano shows a court messenger stopping to reply to a text message on a smartphone. This inconsistency is best described as...
questions.explanation: Anachronism is the placing of an object, custom or idea outside its proper historical period, as with a smartphone in pre-colonial Kano. An aside is a private dramatic remark, while a flashback presents an earlier event and a climax is the point of greatest tension.

questions.q: In a novel, Funmi is calm and cautious while her brother Tunde is reckless. Funmi's calmness mainly throws Tunde's rashness into relief. Funmi is best described as...
questions.explanation: A foil is a character whose qualities contrast with and thereby highlight those of another character. Funmi's caution sets off Tunde's recklessness, whereas a stock character is a conventional type and an antihero lacks conventional heroic qualities.

questions.passage:
At dusk we stood where Gboko market ends,
Two friends, one purse, one promise on the scale.
He took the blame; the flame of friendship bends.
I kept the naira notes and told the tale
Of how a hungry man may guard his own.
The harmattan came down; our shadows thinned.
He chose the truth, I chose to walk alone,
And still the market dust sings of the wind.
questions.q: The sense of the line 'I kept the naira notes and told the tale' continues directly into 'Of how a hungry man may guard his own.' This device is called...
questions.explanation: Enjambment is the running on of a sentence or sense from one line of poetry into the next without a pause. A caesura is a pause within a line, a refrain is a repeated line or group of lines, and an epigram is a concise, pointed statement.

questions.q: A metrical foot made up of one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed syllables, as at the opening of 'carefully', is called a...
questions.explanation: A dactyl has one stressed syllable followed by two unstressed syllables, which matches the opening of 'carefully'. An iamb is unstressed then stressed, a trochee is stressed then unstressed, and an anapest is two unstressed syllables followed by a stressed one.

questions.q: A song of mourning performed at a burial to express grief and praise the deceased is known as...
questions.explanation: A dirge is a funeral song or lament for the dead. A lullaby soothes a child, a panegyric is praise verse or speech without the funeral lament, and a riddle is a puzzle.

questions.q: A cycle of Yoruba tales in which Ijapa the tortoise repeatedly outwits larger animals is best classified as...
questions.explanation: A trickster tale centres on a cunning character, such as Ijapa, who uses wit to outsmart stronger animals. An etiological tale explains the origin of a natural feature or custom, an epic celebrates heroic deeds, and a riddle is a puzzle to be solved.

questions.q: The fixed phrase 'the lion of Benin' used each time an oral epic mentions its hero is an example of...
questions.explanation: A stock epithet is a repeated descriptive phrase attached to a character, often helping oral performers remember and identify the hero. A refrain is a repeated line or group of lines, while an aside and a stage direction belong to drama.

questions.q: A festival performance in Ile-Ife in which masked actors dance and chant to honour a deity, enacting a ritual rather than a realistic story, is best described as...
questions.explanation: Ritual drama grows out of religious or community ceremony and enacts symbolic actions, as in masked dance and chant before a deity. Farce is physical comedy, comedy of manners satirizes social behaviour, and melodrama heightens emotion at the expense of realistic character.

questions.q: A short play performed by characters within the main play, as when a village troupe stages a sketch for the chief, is called...
questions.explanation: A play-within-a-play is a smaller dramatic performance embedded in the larger action. A soliloquy is a speech revealing a character's thoughts alone on stage, an aside is a brief private remark to the audience, and a flashback dramatizes an earlier event.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech in the sentence: 'The generator cleared its throat before the science fair began.'
questions.explanation: The generator is given the human action of clearing its throat, so it is personified. There is no comparison with like or as, which rules out a simile, and the expression is not a word that imitates sound.

questions.q: What figure of speech is used in 'The science fair turned the whole school into a beehive'?
questions.explanation: The school is described as a beehive without using like or as, creating an implied comparison between a busy fair and a hive. A simile would require an explicit comparison, while metonymy would substitute a related name for something else.

questions.passage:
Science Fair Morning

The hall wears bunting, red and white,
and desks have grown strange gardens overnight:
a volcano of clay, a wire sun,
bean seedlings stretching toward the window's light.
Amaka checks her battery twice,
then tells the judge how salt can make ice.
Outside, the school bell argues with the wind;
inside, small bulbs wake one by one.
The trophy waits like a shy guest by the door,
and every pupil's shadow leans to learn.
Through all the noise, her mother's voice returns:
'Measure again. A true result will hold.'
questions.q: In the poem, the phrase 'desks have grown strange gardens overnight' mainly conveys that
options: real plants have mysteriously sprouted on the desks during the night
the pupils have allowed weeds to overtake their neglected desks
the science fair has made the classroom feel more like a farm than a school
the classroom displays have turned into a variety of science projects
questions.explanation: The phrase is a metaphor for the transformed desks, which now hold projects such as a clay volcano and bean seedlings. It does not report an actual overnight growth of plants, and it does not criticise neglect or say the room has become a farm.

Through all the noise, her mother's voice returns:
'Measure again. A true result will hold.'
questions.q: The contrast between the school bell that 'argues with the wind' and the bulbs that 'wake one by one' chiefly emphasises
options: the restless noise outside against the delicate activity of the exhibits inside
the pupils' fear that their projects will not work
the weakness of electric light compared with natural light
the judges' impatience with the noise from the field
questions.explanation: The bell outside is noisy and contentious, while the bulbs inside come alive in a small, orderly way, so the contrast is between outer commotion and inner activity. The lines do not mention the pupils' fear, the judges' impatience, or a judgement about natural light.

questions.q: The line 'The trophy waits like a shy guest by the door' is effective mainly because it
options: shows that the trophy is ignored and considered worthless by everyone
proves that the pupils are too shy to collect their awards
reveals that an outside visitor will be given the prize
makes the trophy seem modest and almost human as it waits to be claimed
questions.explanation: The simile gives the trophy a quiet, hesitant presence, as though it is modestly waiting for its winner. The line does not say the trophy is worthless, that a visitor will receive it, or that the pupils are afraid to collect it.

questions.q: A novel opens with the final moments of a village festival, then returns to the preparations made during the previous week. This arrangement is an example of
questions.explanation: The narrative moves from the festival's end back to earlier events, which is a flashback. Foreshadowing would hint at later events, while suspense would create anxious uncertainty about what happens next.

questions.q: A story about a school science fair is told entirely through letters and text messages exchanged by pupils and their teacher. This narrative form is best described as
questions.explanation: An epistolary narrative is built from letters or similar documents such as messages. A picaresque follows a roguish adventurer, an allegorical story carries a second symbolic meaning, and omniscient narration uses a narrator who knows everything.

questions.passage: Ada stood at the edge of the compound as the drums called the village to the New Yam Festival. She had carried the first yam from her mother's farm in a raffia basket, refusing the help of her younger brothers. Now, watching the elders pour palm wine on the soil, she felt the weight of the basket again—not in her arms, but in her chest. Her mother had said the festival was a thanksgiving for what the earth had given; Ada thought it was also a way of remembering those who had knelt on that same soil before them. When the masquerade appeared, she did not run with the children. She stayed, holding her grandmother's old wrapper tighter around her shoulders.
questions.q: From the passage, Ada's carrying of the first yam without help most strongly suggests that she
options: hopes to receive a special reward from the elders
feels a personal sense of responsibility and pride in the festival
is afraid that the masquerade will chase her away
doubts that her younger brothers are strong enough to lift the basket
questions.explanation: Ada refuses help and later feels the weight 'in her chest,' which connects the yam to her deep sense of duty and belonging. Nothing in the passage says she doubts her brothers' strength, expects a reward, or fears being chased.

questions.passage: Ada stood at the edge of the compound as the drums called the village to the New Yam Festival. Her mother had said the festival was a thanksgiving for what the earth had given; Ada thought it was also a way of remembering those who had knelt on that same soil before them. When the masquerade appeared, she did not run with the children. She stayed, holding her grandmother's old wrapper tighter around her shoulders.
questions.q: The detail that Ada holds her grandmother's old wrapper tighter mainly serves to
options: suggest that she is impatient to leave the festival
show that the harmattan is unusually cold during the festival
reveal that she regrets not running with the other children
link her to family and tradition at a moment of communal remembrance
questions.explanation: The wrapper is associated with her grandmother and is held at the moment she reflects on those who came before, so the gesture suggests continuity and belonging. The passage does not mention cold weather, regret about not running, or a wish to leave.

questions.q: A reference in a literary work to a well-known person, event or another text is called
questions.explanation: An allusion is an indirect reference that relies on the reader's shared knowledge of a person, event or text. An illusion is a false perception, while an allegory is a sustained symbolic narrative, not a brief reference.

questions.q: The use of two contradictory words placed side by side for effect, as in 'living death', is an example of
questions.explanation: Oxymoron joins apparently opposite words to create a striking effect. A paradox is a contradictory statement that may be true in a deeper sense, while metonymy and litotes are different figures of substitution and understatement.

questions.q: A novel told mainly through letters, diaries or other documents is best described as
questions.explanation: An epistolary novel uses letters, diaries or similar documents to present its story. A picaresque novel follows the adventures of a rogue, while an allegorical novel carries a sustained symbolic meaning.

questions.passage:
The maize fields crack beneath the sun,
The well has shrunk to mud and stone;
The women wait, their work undone,
And pray for rain with every moan.

The children scan the brazen sky,
The goats bleat low beside the gate;
A single cloud goes drifting by,
Then disappears—too small, too late.
questions.q: Which rhyme pattern best describes the poem as printed?
questions.explanation: In each stanza, the first and third lines rhyme, and the second and fourth rhyme: sun/undone and stone/moan, then sky/by and gate/late. This gives the pattern abab repeated in both stanzas; abba would require the second and third lines to rhyme with each other.

questions.q: Each stanza of the poem is best described as a
questions.explanation: A quatrain is a stanza of four lines, and the excerpt consists of two four-line stanzas. A couplet has two lines, a sestet six and an octave eight.

questions.q: A line of verse made up of five metrical feet is called
questions.explanation: The prefix penta- means five, so a line of five metrical feet is pentameter. Tetrameter has four feet, hexameter six and trimeter three.

questions.q: In an Efik folktale, the tortoise repeatedly uses cunning to trick other animals and is finally punished for his greed. In oral literature, this character is best described as a
questions.explanation: A trickster figure is a recurring character, often an animal, whose cunning and mischief drive the plot and usually bring eventual punishment. A foil contrasts with another character, while a chorus comments collectively in drama.

questions.q: A play that dramatises actual historical events and uses documentary material to comment on present-day corruption in Enugu is best described as
questions.explanation: Docudrama blends documentary or historical material with dramatic reconstruction, often to comment on contemporary issues. Farce relies on absurd situations and physical humour, while a masque is a courtly entertainment with music and spectacle.

questions.q: In a serious scene where a bride mourns her lost child, the playwright inserts a brief joking exchange between two servants to ease the audience's tension. This technique is called
questions.explanation: Comic relief is a humorous episode introduced into a serious work to relieve tension and heighten the surrounding seriousness. Dramatic irony depends on the audience knowing more than a character, while catharsis is the emotional purging felt at the end of tragedy.

questions.q: Identify the figure of speech in the sentence: 'The nurse's words were a balm to the anxious family.'
questions.explanation: The words are directly described as 'a balm', suggesting healing comfort without using 'like' or 'as'; this direct comparison is metaphor. A simile would require an explicit comparison word, while hyperbole would be deliberate exaggeration.

questions.q: A short story begins with a tense fight at a motor park, then moves to a paragraph explaining how the two men missed the same bus the previous week. This technique is best described as...
questions.explanation: The narrative interrupts the present scene to present an earlier event, which is a flashback. Foreshadowing would hint at later events, while suspense is the feeling of anxious uncertainty.

questions.q: A novelist introduces Bello as a generous trader by showing him quietly paying a stranger's fare at the motor park. This method of characterisation is...
questions.explanation: The reader learns Bello's generosity through his action rather than through a direct statement by the narrator. Interior monologue would reveal his private thoughts, while authorial intrusion would be the narrator commenting openly.

questions.passage:
The night ferry leans into the river,
its engine muttering old prayers;
lanterns hang like low, tired moons
over baskets of yam and sleeping traders.
A child asks the water where the road has gone,
and the water answers only with its knocking.
By dawn, Onitsha rises from mist
with the market already clearing its throat,
and we step out, stiff as new calabashes,
our fare counted twice in the conductor's palm.
questions.q: The simile in 'lanterns hang like low, tired moons' mainly helps to convey the...
options: dim, drooping quality of the lanterns at night
enormous size of the traders' baskets
harsh brightness of the midday sun
questions.explanation: The comparison of the lanterns to low, tired moons suggests faint light hanging downward in the dark. It does not primarily describe the baskets, the ferry's speed or midday brightness.

questions.q: The expression 'the market already clearing its throat' mainly suggests that the market is...
options: preparing to close for the day
questions.explanation: 'Clearing its throat' personifies the market and suggests the first sounds of activity as dawn breaks. The surrounding line places this at daybreak, not at closing time.

questions.q: The image 'we step out, stiff as new calabashes' chiefly conveys the passengers'...
options: stiffness after a long, cramped journey
questions.explanation: The simile compares the passengers' rigid bodies to firm new calabashes after the night journey. It emphasises physical stiffness, not wealth, fear or anger.

questions.passage: When Uncle Emeka rose to speak at the family gathering, the jollof rice was already steaming in the centre of the table. 'A shared meal,' he said, 'is not mere food. It is a meeting of hands, a school of patience, and a treaty signed without paper. Whoever eats alone may fill the stomach, but they leave the heart hungry. See how the pot has gathered us: the trader and the teacher, the driver and the nurse, all reaching for the same dish. Let us not hurry to leave this table. The food that is eaten in conversation stays longer in the memory than the food that is swallowed in silence.' The children, who had waited two hours, looked at one another, and then at the lid still covering the meat.
questions.q: Uncle Emeka's main argument about a shared meal is that it...
options: strengthens human bonds and memory beyond mere feeding
is less important than the food itself
should be eaten quickly before it gets cold
teaches children to wait for two hours
questions.explanation: He calls a shared meal a meeting of hands and a treaty without paper, and says food eaten in conversation remains in memory. His point is about social and emotional nourishment, not speed, the food's lesser value, or a lesson in waiting.

questions.q: The expression 'a treaty signed without paper' chiefly suggests that shared eating...
options: creates unity and agreement among people
is a way of avoiding conversation
questions.explanation: The metaphor of a treaty implies peace and agreement, while 'without paper' shows that the bond is social rather than legal. The passage stresses togetherness and conversation, not avoidance or business formality.

questions.q: The final sentence about the children mainly serves to...
options: contrast the speaker's high sentiments with the children's ordinary hunger
create fear about the covered meat
prove that the children dislike jollof rice
show that Uncle Emeka is cruel
questions.explanation: The children have waited two hours and look at the covered meat, introducing a humorous contrast with Uncle Emeka's lofty speech. The detail does not show dislike of the rice, cruelty, or fear.

questions.q: In a novel, the narrator describes what Chief Nwosu is thinking in his bedroom while also revealing what his daughter is secretly planning in the kitchen. The narrative point of view is best described as...
questions.explanation: A third-person omniscient narrator stands outside the story but knows the thoughts and feelings of several characters. A limited narrator would be restricted mainly to one character's mind.

questions.q: In a play, Chidi is honest and cautious, while his friend Emeka is reckless and impulsive. Emeka's character is made clearer through his contrast with Chidi. Chidi is best described as Emeka's...
questions.explanation: A foil is a character whose contrasting qualities highlight another character's traits. An antagonist actively opposes someone, while a double resembles or mirrors another character.

questions.passage:
At night I read beside the shelf,
And learn the words to know myself;
The pages turn and softly glow,
The dusty volumes round me grow.
questions.q: The end-rhyme scheme of the stanza is...
questions.explanation: The first and second lines rhyme ('shelf' with 'myself'), while the third and fourth rhyme ('glow' with 'grow'); this gives a paired rhyme arrangement.

questions.passage:
At night I read beside the shelf,
And learn the words to know myself;
The pages turn and softly glow,
The dusty volumes round me grow.
questions.q: The regular rhythm of the stanza is best described as...
questions.explanation: Each line has four feet, and each foot generally moves from an unstressed syllable to a stressed one, as in 'at NIGHT' and 'I READ'. This is the iambic pattern, and four feet make tetrameter.
